postData.content:
was thinking about learning an indian language, just in case

but i’m told it’s not the one
what should i actually learn, just in case?

comments.text: English is used everywhere in Indian schools and corporations. There is one state in India where no one speaks or even learns Hindi (TN). If there is one language that unites all Indians, it is ironically English.
I guess I'll need to study english then

Hindi is to relate with the elites. 

Tamil is to relate with the masses.
Hindi is obviously a good choice if you are serious, despite all the political issues here.
I'm Tamilian and say you were told wrong. Hindi is the right language to learn. And then if you spend a significant time in a state in India learn some 'courtesy words' from that state's language.
Learn kannada. Most useful language in Bangalore, the tech capital of India.
What's the purpose? If there is no purpose, directly go to Sanskirt. Forking towards a bulk of Indian languages if you know Sanskrit is very easy.

Learn Hindi. People fight in India over language. But most people still understand it in every part of india as well as in all our neighbouring countries up to the gulf. 

Don't listen to language propaganda creators.
Gujarati. They own half of India. In another 10 years, they will own all of it.
Just learn Hindi dude keep it simple. Even if you are in the East, super north, South etc. at least 1/3 people will know some Hindi.

Maybe try learning vocabulary of sanskrit, largely most Indic languages have root words derived from it. Pepper those words with English conjunctions, adjectives and adverbs. Then you can know, Hinglish, Kanadlish, Tammilish, Punjaish and what not

Hindi is the only one that is useful for an outsider.  Most media (news, films, TV shows, music) is in Hindi.  Verbally, Urdu is almost the same as Hindi so you get a two-fer for verbal communication too (though not reading/writing).  

However, I will say that anyone who speaks

As a south indian. Trust me its hindi.

Sanskrit is a meme answer but if you want to study one as comparative linguistics and not spoken then its a good candidate

Can learn telugu for fun too if you want cause movies from tollywood have been getting famous like RRR and bahubali

India has 22 scheduled languages which are almost difficult to learn all. But if you need to reach masses Hindi is preferred (especially for north India).   

Ranking based on Native speakers 
- Hindi : 528.3 Million  
- Bengali : 97.2 million 
- Marathi : 83.0 million

postData.author: Marc Lou
postData.content:
I was drowning in hundreds of support messages on TrustMRR.

So I made a simple change: support is now reserved for paid customers ($1 minimum)

Everyone else gets the FAQ + a $1 unlock button

It filters out 95% of noise, so paying customers actually get helped faster now.

comments.text: a $1 tax is the best thing to do, If they won’t pay the price of a stick of gum to talk to a human, they aren't a customer they’re just a distraction.
Ever thought of adding AI-assist-only support feature for free, and the human support for $1?

Yes, people insisted on talking to a human so the AI gave up at some point 

AI trained on FAQ so it was pretty good
I would charge more than $1, because once you charge $1 you basically commit to help
yes true
How much do you pay for transaction fee for $1 support? It they dispute this?

prob 0.36?

yeah disputes suck
Good ! Next is auto filter with AI
I had Crisp AI set up too but people kept asking to chat with human and eventually AI turned me in

@marclou
 I paid the 29$ listing fee and still got this pop up.. is that on purpose?
dm ing you

This is genius. Solo founders get crushed by support from free users who will never convert.

I run 13 AI tools and was spending more time on "how do I sign up" emails than building features. The $1 filter is basically a seriousness gate. Stealing this.
Smart move. Support can be a huge drain when building lean. This gets paying customers the focus they deserve.

$1 is a good filter. Beats what I was encountering with Google yesterday where the error I was encountering while upgrading to a paid plan was something it wouldn’t connect me to a human for because I’m not on a paid plan. I’m trying to pay you!
